To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the partial probabilities of the process of Compton effect in magnetized plasma were obtained.
the partial cross section of the Compton scattering in a plasma is strongly suppressed in a strong magnetic fields.
the Compton scattering probability in a strongly magnetize plasma is strongly suppressed in comparison with the splitting probability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Compton scattering in magnetized plasma of arbitrary temperature.
the process of Compton effect in the presence of a magnetic field.
the process of Compton $\gamma e^+ \to \gamma' e^+$ scattering on the electron in the strong magnetic field of the neutron stars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the process of Compton $\gamma e^+e^-\to \gamma e^{+\prime}e^-$ scattering in a strongly magnetised medium is not important for the photon spectrum formation in the strong magnetic fields of the neutron stars and magnetars, but can be essential for the photon spectrum in the pulsars and magnetars with a relatively weak field.

the Compton scattering is a very effective process of energy dissipation for photons with the energy of the order of the electron mass or more, in a strongly magnetised medium with the magnetic field of the order of $10^{12}-10^{14}$ Gauss.
Compton scattering in the presence of a magnetic field is an important mechanism for the energy redistribution in the plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Compton scattering in a magnetized plasma is an important process for the description of the photon propagation in a strong magnetic fields.
in the case of the strong magnetic field the Compton scattering probability is much greater than the probability of photon splitting.
the process of Compton effect in the magnetized plasma is more probable than the photon splitting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Compton scattering probability in a magnetized medium is much smaller than the probability of photon splitting in the same conditions.
Compton scattering of photons in the presence of a strong magnetic field is an efficient channel for the energy transfer between photons and plasma electrons in the magnetar magnetosphere.
the Compton scattering in the magnetized plasma is a process that should be considered for a proper interpretation of the observed spectra of magnetized astrophysical objects.
